# Workflow Documentation

Building on @fig-agent-architecture, this chapter describes the workflow from the customer's perspective and highlights the main processing steps where helpful. For a new customer,
the journey begins with onboarding, where they
provide personal information and answer questions about their mobility situation and preferences. They can review and update these answers at any time by editing
their profile, which triggers a fresh analysis. The profile also shows active and inactive subscriptions for context, but they cannot be changed there. When
the customer opens the dashboard, the system combines their current subscriptions, trips from the most recent twelve months of available history, the stored catalogue
of available plans, and, if shared, their calendar.

The customer then receives an analysis of their current mobility portfolio. For every category of transport they use, the system calculates what they spent
during the twelve-month period and compares their current subscription with eligible alternatives. Prices and savings come from the deterministic analysis engine, keeping the figures
reproducible (see ADR-02). The dashboard presents annual mobility spending, the CO~2~ footprint, mode distribution, current subscriptions, potential savings, and the recommended portfolio. After reviewing
the initial results, the customer can explore forward-looking recommendations for the next twelve months. The system combines seasonal travel patterns with shared calendar entries
to estimate how travel might change. Where it fits the customer's priorities and mobility constraints, it may recommend switching transport modes, for example from
an e-scooter to a bicycle or from a car to public transport. These suggestions weigh cost, CO~2~ emissions, and estimated travel time, which serves
as the current proxy for flexibility, according to the customer's selected priorities. The language model assesses future demand and the feasibility of a modal
shift, while the deterministic engine calculates the resulting costs. The Advisor chat built into the dashboard opens with a short summary of the findings.
The customer can ask why a plan is cheaper or about its cancellation terms, and the Advisor can consult the stored product catalogue and
underlying tariff documents. It can also simulate scenarios such as "what if I switch to nextbike" without changing the stored portfolio.

Finally, if the customer decides to make a change, the Advisor presents a preview of how the proposed switch or cancellation would affect the
portfolio and its costs. The customer can reject it, continue exploring alternatives, or proceed to a separate explicit confirmation. Only after this confirmation is
a revised recommendation stored in a new internal analysis-session snapshot (see ADR-03). The underlying subscription record remains unchanged, and the current prototype does not
place or cancel a real subscription with an external mobility provider.
